cases.sentence: ___ стояли в необычных белых костюмах, полностью закрывавших тело
cases.translation: The soldiers stood in unusual white suits that completely covered their bodies.
cases.explain: Солдаты is the subject of the verb стояли (stood), so it is in the Nominative plural.

cases.sentence: Мы живем в военном городке у ___, закрытого наукограда
cases.translation: We live in a military town near Obninsk, a closed science city.
cases.explain: The preposition у ("near/by") governs the Genitive case, so Обнинск becomes Обнинска.

cases.sentence: Надежным способом считалось просто подъехать к ___ и высыпать патроны с моста
cases.translation: A reliable method was thought to be simply driving up to the river and dumping cartridges off the bridge.
cases.explain: The preposition к ("toward") governs the Dative case, so речка becomes речке.

cases.sentence: ___ стали выселять из 30-километровой зоны вокруг атомной станции
cases.translation: People began to be evacuated from the 30-kilometer zone around the nuclear plant.
cases.explain: Людей is the direct object of выселять (to evacuate); for animate plural nouns the Accusative matches the Genitive form.

cases.sentence: Их дом, первый в деревне, крышу которого покрыли ___
cases.translation: Their house, the first in the village, had its roof covered with iron sheeting.
cases.explain: The Instrumental expresses the material used for covering ("with iron"), so железо becomes железом.

cases.translation: My father was born in this village.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating location governs the Prepositional case, so село becomes селе.

cases.sentence: Надежным способом считалось просто подъехать к речке и высыпать патроны с ___
cases.translation: A reliable method was simply to drive up to the river and dump the cartridges off the bridge.
cases.explain: The preposition с here meaning "off/from" governs the Genitive case, so мост becomes моста.

cases.sentence: Деньги, согласно семейной ___, пропили в сельсовете
cases.translation: The money, according to family legend, was drunk away at the village council.
cases.explain: The preposition-like word согласно ("according to") governs the Dative case, so легенда becomes легенде.

reading.ru: Солдаты стояли в необычных белых костюмах, полностью закрывавших тело.
reading.question: What were the soldiers wearing when young Alexei saw them from the car?
options: White protective suits covering their whole bodies
reading.correct: White protective suits covering their whole bodies
reading.explain: The chapter opens with soldiers in "необычных белых костюмах, полностью закрывавших тело".

reading.ru: Мне девять лет.
reading.question: How old was Alexei when he witnessed the soldiers checking cars for radiation?
reading.correct: Nine
reading.explain: He states plainly "Мне девять лет".

reading.ru: Это происходит потому, что недавно был взрыв на Чернобыльской атомной станции
reading.question: What event explained the soldiers' presence checking cars on the road?
options: The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear plant
reading.correct: The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear plant
reading.explain: His parents explain it's because "недавно был взрыв на Чернобыльской атомной станции".

reading.ru: Хотя каждый дурак в нашем городе знает, добавила мама, что настоящая причина совсем в другом.
reading.question: According to Alexei's mother, was the official explanation for the radiation checks true?
options: No, she said everyone knew the real reason was different
She had no opinion on it
She said it was classified information
reading.correct: No, she said everyone knew the real reason was different
reading.explain: His mother adds that "настоящая причина совсем в другом" (the real reason was something else entirely).

reading.ru: Мой отец родился в этом селе.
reading.question: Where was Alexei's father born?
options: In the village of Zalesye near Chernobyl
reading.correct: In the village of Zalesye near Chernobyl
reading.explain: The text says his father was born in the village of Zalesye, near the Chernobyl station: "Мой отец родился в этом селе".

reading.ru: Их читала религиозная бабушка, а я просто запоминал и мог повторить, не понимая смысла.
reading.question: What did Alexei's religious grandmother teach him during his summer visits to Ukraine?
options: Prayers, which he memorized without understanding
reading.correct: Prayers, which he memorized without understanding
reading.explain: His grandmother recited prayers that he "запоминал и мог повторить, не понимая смысла".

reading.ru: В ней меня крестили тайком от отца.
reading.question: What secret did Alexei's grandmother keep from his atheist military-officer father?
options: She secretly had him baptized in church
reading.correct: She secretly had him baptized in church
reading.explain: He was baptized in the local church, "тайком от отца" (secretly, from his father).

reading.ru: Рай был уничтожен в половину второго ночи 26 апреля 1986 года.
reading.question: When did the Chernobyl reactor explosion occur?
reading.correct: 1:30 a.m. on April 26, 1986
reading.explain: He states the disaster happened "в половину второго ночи 26 апреля 1986 года".

reading.ru: жители сел вокруг Чернобыля, включая моих родственников, выгнали на сельскохозяйственные работы сажать картошку.
reading.question: What did authorities force villagers near Chernobyl to do days after the explosion, despite knowing the danger?
options: Go out and plant potatoes in the fields
Wear protective gear at all times
reading.correct: Go out and plant potatoes in the fields
reading.explain: Villagers, including his relatives, "выгнали на сельскохозяйственные работы сажать картошку".

reading.ru: В Киеве, огромном миллионном городе и столице Украины, 1 мая, то есть спустя всего 5 дней после взрыва, была проведена первомайская демонстрация.
reading.question: What propaganda event was held in Kyiv just five days after the explosion?
reading.correct: The May Day parade
reading.explain: Kyiv held its "первомайская демонстрация" (May Day demonstration) only five days after the disaster.

reading.ru: Всего под выселение попало 116 тысяч человек.
reading.question: How many people were evacuated because of the Chernobyl disaster, according to the text?
reading.explain: The text states "Всего под выселение попало 116 тысяч человек".

reading.ru: А на чердаке у моей бабушки сушилась рыба.
reading.question: What object caused a memorable family incident during the evacuation?
options: Dried fish left in the attic that the grandmother mailed away
A radio hidden under the floor
reading.correct: Dried fish left in the attic that the grandmother mailed away
reading.explain: Fish drying "на чердаке у моей бабушки" led her to mail it home rather than abandon it.

reading.ru: Рыба фонила так, будто на нее сбросили атомную бомбу.
reading.question: What happened when Alexei's father tested the mailed fish with a radiation detector?
options: It had gone bad but wasn't radioactive
reading.correct: It was extremely radioactive
reading.explain: The fish "фонила так, будто на нее сбросили атомную бомбу" (was as radioactive as if a bomb had hit it).

reading.ru: Всемогущий, прекрасно известный всей стране, шутка ли, 20 лет во главе министерства, министр внутренних дел Щелоков потеряет все и застрелится.
reading.question: What ultimately happened to the powerful Interior Minister Shchyolokov in the metro murder story?
options: He lost everything and shot himself
He was promoted to General Secretary
reading.correct: He lost everything and shot himself
reading.explain: The text states minister Shchyolokov "потеряет все и застрелится" (would lose everything and shoot himself).

reading.ru: Афанасьева запихнули в служебную Волгу, отвезли в подмосковный лес, где забили металлической арматурой и бросили.
reading.question: What did the drunken policemen do to KGB Major Afanasyev after robbing him of his sausage and cognac?
options: They beat him with metal rebar and left him in the forest
They released him with an apology
They took him to a hospital
reading.correct: They beat him with metal rebar and left him in the forest
reading.explain: They drove him to a forest "где забили металлической арматурой и бросили".

reading.ru: Многие до сих пор вспоминают Андропова с ностальгией
reading.question: How do many people in the security services still regard Andropov, according to Navalny?
options: With nostalgia, as a wise leader who restored order
reading.correct: With nostalgia, as a wise leader who restored order
reading.explain: He writes that "Многие до сих пор вспоминают Андропова с ностальгией", building a myth around him.

reading.ru: Когда умер Брежнев, мать плакала.
reading.question: How did Alexei's mother react to Brezhnev's death?
options: She cried, even though she didn't especially love him
She was afraid of the news
reading.correct: She cried, even though she didn't especially love him
reading.explain: He recalls "Когда умер Брежнев, мать плакала", though she hadn't especially loved him.

reading.ru: Кто с ума сошел? — кричит она мне.
reading.question: Why did young Alexei's mother rush home in a panic on the day Brezhnev died?
options: Because he played loud rock music the same day
Because he was late from school
reading.correct: Because he played loud rock music the same day
reading.explain: She rushed in shouting "Кто с ума сошел?" because he had blasted music through the open window on the day of national mourning.

reading.ru: Значимой идеологической диверсией, повлиявшей на меня и превратившей в маленького диссидента, была музыка.
reading.question: What does Navalny credit as a major influence in turning him into a young dissident?
reading.correct: Rock music
reading.explain: He states that the key ideological influence "была музыка" (was music), specifically rock.

reading.ru: Одним из главных отрицательных примеров, призванных оттолкнуть советских телезрителей от тлетворного влияния Запада, была группа КИС.
reading.question: Which band did Soviet TV single out as a negative example, misreading its name as Nazi-related?
reading.correct: KISS
reading.explain: Soviet propaganda targeted "группа КИС" (the band KISS), claiming its name referenced Nazi SS units.

reading.ru: Мне достался бумажный пакетик сахара из самолета с английской надписью «Аэрофлот».
reading.question: What souvenir did young Alexei receive from a family friend who had traveled abroad?
options: A paper sugar packet from an airplane with an English label
reading.correct: A paper sugar packet from an airplane with an English label
reading.explain: He treasured "бумажный пакетик сахара из самолета с английской надписью «Аэрофлот»".

reading.ru: Жевательной резинкой, их главным детским сокровищем.
reading.question: What was the ultimate childhood status symbol among kids whose fathers had served abroad?
reading.correct: Imported chewing gum
reading.explain: Classmates proved their fathers' foreign service with "жевательной резинкой, их главным детским сокровищем" (chewing gum, their main childhood treasure).

reading.ru: В СССР секса не было, вот каждый хотел привезти его кусочек из-за границы.
reading.question: How does Navalny explain the Soviet obsession with erotic calendars and souvenirs brought from abroad?
options: The joke that "there was no sex in the USSR," so people craved a piece of it from abroad
reading.correct: The joke that "there was no sex in the USSR," so people craved a piece of it from abroad
reading.explain: He explains it plainly: "В СССР секса не было, вот каждый хотел привезти его кусочек из-за границы".

reading.ru: Но кто же будет вспоминать неудобные резиновые сапоги, грязь под ногтями и ощущение полной бессмысленности собственного труда
reading.question: What does Navalny say people conveniently forget when nostalgically recalling mandatory potato-harvesting trips?
options: The uncomfortable boots, dirt, and pointlessness of the work
The good food they were given
reading.correct: The uncomfortable boots, dirt, and pointlessness of the work
reading.explain: He asks who would remember "неудобные резиновые сапоги, грязь под ногтями и ощущение полной бессмысленности собственного труда".

reading.ru: но все-таки главное мое детское воспоминание об СССР — очередь за молоком.
reading.question: What does Navalny call his single most important childhood memory of the USSR?
reading.correct: Standing in line for milk
reading.explain: He states his "главное детское воспоминание об СССР — очередь за молоком" (main childhood memory of the USSR is the line for milk).
